intended_claim: One declared standard-model muscle-tendon tension solution for prescribed movement and external loading

items.current: Generic 180 cm / 90 kg reference with standard segment fractions and muscle parameters. Individual measurements are not required for this project.
items.effect: Single muscle-reference multipliers can be changed while the standard body is held fixed. This is not an individual anatomy reconstruction.

items.current: Rigid segments, native joint axes and ROM, coordinate couplers; anatomical muscle and joint connectivity must support the prescribed movement.
items.effect: No deformable bone, explicit cartilage contact, independent ligament mechanics or freely moving native scapula.

items.current: 416 force elements with attachment/via/wrapping paths; visual mesh count and shape are separate. Thirty derivative checks across six independent coordinates and 416 elements pass in the current converted model.
items.effect: Force elements are not 416 independent anatomical whole muscles. Geometry and moment arms must be checked over each task ROM. Native lower-limb conversion notes report knee moment-arm differences from OpenSim; derivative consistency does not establish anatomical fidelity.

items.current: Trapezius, serratus anterior, rhomboids and levator scapulae force paths are missing from the active whole-body backend. Replacement shoulder component remains unintegrated.
items.effect: Scapular work and stabilization cannot be assigned to their actual muscles; coupled shoulder work can be misattributed.

items.current: Imported MuJoCo force-length-velocity gain and passive force are evaluated in the jump audit. Current motion dynamics use generalized joint demands.
items.effect: Inherited parameter errors and operating-range issues can invalidate muscle-specific values even when rigid-body balance passes.
items.status: available and audited; not a released jump force solution

items.current: Inelastic tendon and zero pennation in the current backend. Tendon elasticity is an optional extension, not a prerequisite for the first tension reference.
items.effect: No independent tendon recoil prediction; this simplification is accepted for the current tension-only model.

items.current: Library reference forces normalize force sharing. Demand effort e >= 0 has no hard upper bound.
items.effect: Computed demand is not bounded neural activation, firing rate, measured maximum strength, or a prediction that a person can complete the movement.

items.current: A joint task-independent solver selects a temporally continuous reference-normalized tension history with a magnitude regularizer. Physiological minimum effort or metabolic energy is deferred.
items.effect: Magnitude and continuity regularization choose one mathematical history. They do not claim that the nervous system minimizes this objective.

items.current: Active and passive tension enter equilibrium. The new reference solver can enforce the existing generic GH reaction-direction cone. No arbitrary muscle-specific antagonist force floor is inserted.
items.effect: Stability constraints can require additional muscles to carry tension. The GH cone must not be treated as a universal knee/ankle stability model.
items.status: implemented GH approximation; other joint stability rules not supplied

items.current: No firing-rate, activation-history, fiber-type recruitment, fatigue or potentiation model. These are outside the requested scope.
items.effect: No claim about neural activation or fatigue is needed for the requested mechanical tension comparison.

items.current: Gravity 9.80665 m/s²; no air drag; ideal unilateral flat contact; assumed friction coefficient 0.8. Baseline GRF and landing-duration profiles are inputs.
items.effect: Landing peak, jump performance and shoe/floor deformation are not independently predicted. Force-plate profiles are not measured.

items.current: Generated posture targets and contact phases. Vertical reference passes numerical checks at 2400 Hz; large internal transients remain. Long-jump recovery is incomplete.
items.effect: Force balance and convergence do not establish natural human movement or empirical muscle-force accuracy.

items.current: Physical segment similarity scaling changes length, width/depth, inertia and attachment geometry together. Mass and reference force are separate controls.
items.effect: Independent length-only, width and muscle-size/architecture adjustment is not yet implemented. A new body needs refitted motion, contact and muscle-range checks.

items.current: Primary output is muscle-tendon tension in N, with active/passive components. Other mechanical quantities are retained only for checks and constraints.
items.effect: They do not directly provide local tissue stress, cartilage pressure, hypertrophy volume, fatigue or microdamage. A normalized tension ratio is not percentage activation.

items.current: Required checks concern mechanical consistency, path/parameter validity, task continuity and declared force allocation. Empirical and individual calibration remain optional additional confidence, not prerequisites imposed on this generic-model project.
items.effect: A declared mechanical reference solution is the deliverable. Comparisons must retain consistent assumptions and resolve actual geometry or motion defects.

seth.title: Seth et al. 2019 — shoulder muscle contributions

hicks.title: Hicks et al. 2015 — verification and validation

required: rigid segment kinematics and consistent contacts
muscle attachment paths and force-length-velocity/passive laws
accepted_simplifications: generic standard anthropometry and muscle parameters
rigid tendon for the first tension solution
out_of_scope: individual anatomical measurement or personal force prediction
neural firing, fiber-type recruitment and fatigue
local stress, injury or tissue damage
